summary: Approval history at 72b43cd2cc: each sandbox escalation that needs approval writes D24's approval/asked and approval/decided events as synced Pi custom entries of type bake.approval, the request before anyone is asked and the answer before an allowed-once call runs; permissions::history folds them into an audit trail that grants nothing. The tests ran in the rust gates at HEAD 519a202b13, where the approval code and both test files are byte-identical to the candidate: the second full Linux preflight passed 33 gates (actionlint and runtime skipped) after a first attempt under umask 077 failed two packaging gates on an archive mode check, and the Intel x86_64 macOS native preflight passed 4 gates; each rust gate passed the 15 agent_session::approval_tests and the 9 permissions::history::tests. Write failures are injected at the durable write seam, and the kill test kills a held child after its answer is synced. The worker's saved slice-branch logs show a passing workspace test run that includes both test sets, a cross-target Clippy of bake-coding-agent with no diagnostic, a whole-workspace one that exits 1 on another slice's bake-cli test dead code, and one run and one round of 8 concurrent copies of the approval tests, where B's report states 80 runs and 3 rounds; its four mutation controls left no log. Windows (compile-checked only), Apple Silicon, kills between the two entries or inside write or fsync, real ENOSPC or EIO, and Auto review remain.

results.behavior: In the Linux and Intel macOS rust gates at HEAD and in the slice's saved workspace test log: the_request_and_its_answer_are_on_disk_before_the_call_runs passed: the answerer fixture reads the session file when asked and finds exactly the asked entry, and the effect fixture finds asked and decided allowed-once with their exact data (toolName, callId, reason, sandbox workspace-write); the file order is call, asked, decided, result, each the child of the one before, and a reopened file folds to the same record. each_answer_is_recorded_and_answered_as_without_a_record checks allowed-once, rejected, cancelled, and unavailable: the recorded and unrecorded sessions give the same tool result text and isError, the pair holds the answer given, and only allowed-once runs the effect. never_and_no_answerer_still_record_the_pair, allowed_once_covers_only_its_call (two calls, two request ids, each run after its own decided is on disk), a_session_that_does_not_persist_records_nothing, and an_engine_records_into_one_session also passed. The tests run over the faux provider. Counts describe Cargo tests, summed per test binary.

In the Linux and Intel macOS rust gates at HEAD and in the slice's saved workspace test log: an_unwritable_request_refuses_the_call_unasked_and_stops_the_session and an_unwritable_answer_refuses_the_call_and_stops_the_session passed. A Refuse or FailSync fault armed on the asked or the decided line makes the prompt fail with the injected error; the call never runs, no further provider request is made, no tool result lands after the gap, and the next prompt is refused. No one is asked when the asked line fails; an unsynced line stays in the file, including decided allowed-once with no result after it. an_abort_before_the_request_is_admitted_asks_no_one_and_records_nothing, an_abort_before_the_answer_is_admitted_records_cancelled (decided is written as cancelled and the call does not run), and a_shut_down_session_refuses_without_asking also passed. Faults are injected through the cfg(test) group-fault seam; no real ENOSPC or EIO was produced.

In the Linux and Intel macOS rust gates at HEAD and in the slice's saved workspace test log: the_requests_are_the_same_with_and_without_the_entries passed. Through Pi's sandboxed write under read-only and ask, one approved and one rejected escalation give the provider the same captured requests, tools included, in a recorded and an unrecorded session, after every timestamp is zeroed and every durationMs removed; the request rebuilt from the recorded file serializes byte-identically to the one rebuilt from that file with its bake.approval lines removed and their children re-parented. a_reopened_session_asks_again also passed: after reopening a file holding allowed-once for c1, a new escalation asks again and is rejected, its effect never runs, and the permission knobs stay at their default. In the Mac log the first test's ok lands on line 652, after a child test's output, and the bake-coding-agent library's result line reports 947 passed, 0 failed, and 3 ignored.

a_writer_killed_after_the_answer_reopens_with_the_call_unanswered passed on Linux and Intel macOS at HEAD and in the slice's saved workspace test log; approval_writer_child is its child entry point and returns at once in the parent run. The child re-runs the test binary, writes and syncs decided allowed-once, and blocks in the approval_written hook before the effect; the parent asserts it is still running, kills it, and asserts signal 9. The reopened file folds to one allowed-once record for c1 with nothing skipped, the permission knobs are the default, c1 is unanswered, the rebuilt request ends with Pi's synthetic error result No result provided, and the effect's marker file does not exist. The kill lands after the child's own write and sync, not between the two entries or inside a write or fsync system call. The Windows branch, which expects exit code 1, has not run.

permissions::history::tests' 9 tests passed in the Linux and Intel macOS rust gates at HEAD and in the slice's saved workspace test log. Every field of both kinds writes under its TypeScript name and reads back equal for every sandbox mode and outcome; absent optional fields are omitted and null reads as absent; unknown or missing versions and malformed data are errors naming the problem; an aborted asked is not admitted and an aborted decided becomes cancelled; the fold pairs requests with answers by id, leaves an unanswered request without an outcome, and skips and reports an orphan answer, a repeated ask, a second answer, a data-less entry, and a version 2 entry; the permission fold ignores approval entries. In a_damaged_session_file_opens_and_folds the unparseable and torn lines are dropped when the file opens, so the fold reports nothing skipped and keeps the one allowed-once record.

Cross-target Clippy at HEAD ran over the whole workspace, all targets, with -D warnings, for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and aarch64-apple-darwin. In both passes it re-checked bake-coding-agent, with bake-sandbox, bake-tui, and bake-cli, the other crates being fresh, and it ended exit 0 with no warning or error, so the approval code and tests, including the kill test's Windows branch, compile and lint for both targets. Nothing ran on Windows or Apple Silicon.
The approval entries, failed-write refusals, and the killed writer on Windows, including its expected exit code 1.
